name: Starn

attributes.attribute: the name of two obscure Irish figures
a leader of the early settlement of Ireland
a poet linked to the line of Nemed

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Starn is the name of two obscure Irish heroes. The myth gives them little to do. One Starn is said to be a brother of Partholón, the leader who brought people to Ireland in the early tales. The other Starn is a son of Nemed. In that line he is the father of the poet Tuan mac Cairill. Koch adds a trace of the name. A later old tale makes Partholón the son of a man named Starn. The same tale calls Partholón a Greek. The two Starns sit on the edge of the Irish foundation legends. Their names carry the line of the early peoples even when the stories do not unfold them fully.
